question: Two poles of height 6 m and 11 m stand vertically upright on a plane ground. If the distance between their foot is 12 m, then the distance between their top is:-
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance between tops = √[(Height Difference)² + (Horizontal Distance)²]

⇒ Distance = √[(11 − 6)² + 12²]

⇒ Distance = √[5² + 12²]

⇒ Distance = √[25 + 144] = √169 = 13 m

**∴ The correct answer is 13 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of the first pole (AB) = 6 m

Height of the second pole (CD) = 11 m

Distance between their foot (BD) = 12 m

**Formula Used:**

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let us draw a line AE parallel to the ground BD, meeting the taller pole at E.

⇒ Because ABDE forms a rectangle, AE = BD = 12 m

⇒ ED = AB = 6 m

⇒ The remaining height CE = CD − ED = 11 − 6 = 5 m

⇒ In right-angled ΔAEC, ∠AEC = 90°

⇒ AC² = AE² + CE²

⇒ AC² = 12² + 5²

⇒ AC² = 144 + 25 = 169

⇒ AC = √169 = 13 m

**∴ The correct answer is 13 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagoras Theorem

It states that in a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the perpendicular base and height: a² + b² = c².

Common Pythagorean Triples

Memorizing standard Pythagorean triples like (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (7, 24, 25), and (8, 15, 17) helps in directly calculating the missing side without going through the complete square and root method.

Rectangular Property Application

When solving vertical height differences over a given horizontal span, drawing a perpendicular to the taller vertical breaks the complex shape into a simple rectangle (opposite sides equal) and a right-angled triangle on top.
